newsitem.title: USA: Clinton disappointed at court decision on veto.
newsitem.headline: Clinton disappointed at court decision on veto.

text.p: The White House expressed disappointment Friday at a federal judge's decision to throw out a new law that would give the president power to veto individual spending items from the U.S. budget.
Spokesman Mike McCurry said the White House legal counsel's office was considering what steps can be taken in light of the decision Thursday by U.S. District Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson.
"We are disappointed and we're studying the opinion," he said. He would not comment when asked whether an appeal was being considered.
The so-called line-item veto law was enacted last year by the Republican Congress as part of its Contract with America and was strongly supported by President Clinton, who has yet to use it.
"The president fully intended to use the line-item veto when necessary to protect the interests of U.S. taxpayers," McCurry said.
